outcomeNote: Two exclusions read from the mishna's wording

segments.he: עַל אֵלּוּ הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ. ״עַל אֵלּוּ״ דְּרֵישָׁא לְמַעוֹטֵי עֶצֶם כִּשְׂעוֹרָה, דְּעַל מַגָּעוֹ וְעַל מַשָּׂאוֹ — אִין, וְעַל אֲהִילוֹ — לָא. וְ״עַל אֵלּוּ״ דְּסֵיפָא — לְמַעוֹטֵי אֶבֶן הַסָּכוֹכִית.
segments.en: § The mishna taught that «for» all «these» aforementioned sources of ritual impurity «a nazirite shaves.» The Gemara explains that the phrase: «For these, in» the mishna’s «first clause,» serves «to exclude a bone that is a barley-grain»-«bulk. As for touching it and carrying it, yes,» a nazirite shaves, «but for his overlying» it, «no,» he does not shave. «And» the phrase: «For these, in the» mishna’s «latter clause,» serves «to exclude an overhanging [hasekhukhit] stone.» Although a stone that forms a cover over a corpse imparts impurity in a tent, a nazirite is nevertheless not obligated to shave due to this source of impurity.

moves.summary: First clause excludes overlying a barley-grain bone

moves.summary: Latter clause excludes the overhanging stone
